summary: 161 holdings; the top ten are 31% of the portfolio.
Trades a lot: about 43% of the portfolio changes in a year.
The average holding, by value, has been owned for 4.9 years.
Compared with the typical S&P 500 company, its holdings are similarly priced and much larger.
Copying each filing beat the S&P 500 in 4 of 9 full years.

profile.background: Studied accounting at the University of Minnesota and finance at Wisconsin, then joined Harris Associates, the firm behind the Oakmark Funds, after a spell at Northwestern Mutual. Director of research, then manager of Oakmark Select from 1996, the Oakmark Fund from 2000 and Oakmark Global Select from 2006.
profile.approach: Buys companies trading well below their intrinsic value, often where a short-term problem hides a strong long-term business.
known: Oakmark Select returned 12.8% a year from 1996 to 2017, against 8.1% for the S&P 500 (MoneyWeek, 2017).
profile.note: Harris Associates runs several funds and managers; the 13F combines them all.
